properties.name: A settled question was put to the owner a second time because the requirement's prose still said it was open, three weeks after the Decision that closed it
properties.statement:
OBSERVED 2026-09-09, on reflow2's own design. A session was asked to close the `fix_without_recorded_cause` gap. It read this requirement's statement, whose final paragraph said "NOT YET DECIDED: … whether it is retro-fittable to the 472 events already recorded or … binds only forward. Anthony's own words read as forward-only, but that is his call to make explicitly rather than mine to infer." Taking that at face value, it put the fork to Anthony with three options and a recommendation. He chose forward-only.

THE QUESTION HAD BEEN ANSWERED ON 2026-08-17. `dec:the-patch-record-binds-forward-not-backward` — ACCEPTED, carrying his approver edge, and GOVERNED_BY-linked to this very requirement — says "FORWARD ONLY … no backfill pass will be run over them", with the same reasoning the session reconstructed from scratch. The answers agree, so nothing wrong was built; the cost was the owner being asked a question he had already settled, which is how a person learns the tool is not listening.

⭐ WHY IT WAS NOT CAUGHT, and this is the reusable part rather than the incident. The session did search first — `search_design` for "a fix says whether it corrected the cause repair workaround stands in for" returned twelve hits including the requirement, the rule, the capability, the artifact and the verification, and NOT the governing decision, whose name ("Recording whether a fix reached the cause binds from here…") shares few tokens with the query. The decision was found only incidentally, in the edge list of a snapshot taken for an unrelated write. A BM25 search over what a node SAYS does not reliably surface the node that GOVERNS the one you are reading.

⭐ THE GENERAL CLASS, which every project using reflow2 is exposed to: PROSE ASSERTING AN OPEN QUESTION OUTLIVES THE DECISION THAT SETTLES IT, and nothing notices. reflow2 already recognises this shape one type over — `set_verification_status` returns `prose_currency` when a status moves and the node's description was written under the old one, quoting the prose so a human can judge it. There is no equivalent for a Requirement whose statement claims something is undecided while an ACCEPTED Decision governing it has decided exactly that. The signal is available and cheap: this requirement had a GOVERNED_BY edge to the deciding node the whole time.

NOT A CLAIM THAT PROSE CAN BE CHECKED AUTOMATICALLY FOR TRUTH — it cannot, and `dec:report-dont-judge` forbids reflow2 deciding a paragraph is wrong. The reachable version is narrower and mechanical: when a node carrying phrases like "NOT YET DECIDED" / "still open" / "his call to make" is GOVERNED_BY an accepted Decision, say so and quote both, the way prose_currency does. A reader decides.
